applies_why: This judge text decides D5 versus C5 by whether Isaiah 7:14's sign remains open after the defender answers the almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, rather than by weighing the pressed chain against the defender's chain by footing.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase 'never verse by verse': I weighed whether 'leaving the sign's sense open' is a permissible chain-footing conclusion or an impermissible verse-level open-sense test; I read it as the latter.
why: By resting the underdetermined result on the sign's open sense, the judge applies the retired open/stating-verse test instead of weighing chain against chain by footing as K-C requires.
